text:
Tarik Muharemovic is proving one of the best signings of this Premier League season and there will be special resonance when his upwardly mobile Leeds side host Coventry on Saturday.
Whereas Muharemovic’s father, Rasim, has been a matchday regular since the defender’s £34.1m move from Sassuolo, his mother, Elmedina, will watch her son play for Leeds for the first time.
The 6ft 4in Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-half credits his parents for a rise which has taken him to Wolfsberger in Austria and Juventus and Sassuolo in Italy before he joined Daniel Farke’s side in July. Rasim and Elmedina fled war in their homeland and moved to Slovenia, where Muharemovic and his brother, Kenan, were born.
“My whole story is down to my parents and everything I do is for them,” says the articulate 23-year-old, who speaks five languages and represented Bosnia at this year’s World Cup. “I think about them leaving their home, their family and friends and it was because of a war.
“Bosnia was in a bad situation; the whole of Yugoslavia was in a bad situation so they had to leave. They went to live in Slovenia for three years before moving to Austria because there were better jobs and more opportunities.
“My parents live there now but it’s still not easy when they look back at leaving their home and friends … yet they had to. They do everything for me and Kenan, who is at Rapid Vienna in Austria. He’s only 20 and some of my friends and family say he could be a bigger talent than me. He’s also a left-footed centre-back and we speak every day.”
During Muharemovic’s childhood, his father was relentless in helping him to realise his potential and not much has changed. “My dad would always be there asking: ‘Tarik, if you want to be the best, why didn’t you do this?’” Muharemovic says. “He pushed me to the limits, he was always there on the sidelines and still is now at every Leeds game. I can sometimes hear him shouting from the stands.”
Muharemovic quickly rose to prominence at Wolfsberger and after six first-team appearances he signed for Juventus aged 18 in 2021. He trained with the revered defenders Giorgio Chiellini and Leonardo Bonucci but a first-team appearance eluded Muharemovic and he joined Sassuolo, then in Serie B, initially on loan, in August 2024.
That proved the making of him as they were promoted as champions and Muharemovic thrived under Fabio Grosso’s guidance. He says: “Juventus was the best defensive school with a coach in Massimo Allegri who focused a lot on training and tactics and players like Chiellini and Bonucci.
“As a teenager, it was a privilege to train with these guys because they tell you everything you need to do. Chiellini would celebrate slide tackles and winning duels during games, so I like to do that too because my emotion comes out.
“I’ve always closely followed Virgil van Dijk’s defending and Edin Dzeko is a big idol of mine as a legend of Bosnian football. I’m very honoured and proud to have had such special moments with him, especially representing Bosnia together at the World Cup.”
Muharemovic’s World Cup experiences included a red card against Switzerland and being the victim of a challenge by Folarin Balogun which led to the USA forward being sent off, only for his one-game ban to be suspended by Fifa after an intervention by Donald Trump. The summer also brought interest from Inter and speculation about a return to Juventus before Leeds signed him on a five-year deal.
“I had a few teams interested in me but the dream has always been to play in the Premier League,” says Muharemovic, who captained Bosnia for the first time against Romania this month. “I had an amazing call with the boss [Farke] about the project at Leeds and just had to say yes. He’s built a family here and there’s a huge togetherness with all the players, staff and fans.”
Leeds thumped Chelsea 4-1 last weekend in their first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, prompting talk of a push for European qualification. They have not conceded in the opening 22 minutes in the past 43 matches and belief is growing.
“We all dream about Europe and playing on the big stage,” says Muharemovic, whose performances for Leeds have attracted admiring glances across the continent. “It would be very deserved and special if we can do it for us as players, the fans and the club … I’m just happy with what I’m doing for me and my family and to show those people who didn’t believe in me that I can do it.
“Everyone knows the Premier League is the most difficult league in football but I never doubted myself. I know my qualities and I’m having a good season but it’s very early so I just need to keep playing consistently.”
Looking ahead to his parents’ visit, Muharemovic, a Muslim who prays five times a day, says: “It’ll be very emotional when I see them together at Elland Road for the first time. My dad has been to every game so far and was in the away end in the opening match at Nottingham Forest. I thought the families would sit in a different part of the ground, so when I saw him sat with the Leeds supporters as I was warming up, I was like: ‘Oh my God, good luck!’
“I know what Leeds fans are like so I was thinking: ‘I just hope no one jumps over him,’ but he absolutely loves it. Now my mum is coming too, it’s special and I can’t wait so hopefully we can celebrate with another win. Yes, I’m living the dream but I’m just getting started and always want to show more and achieve more.”
digest_he: טאריק מוחארמוביץ' מתגלה כאחד ההעברות המוצלחות העונה בפרמיירליג במדי לידס יונייטד. לקראת משחק הבית של קבוצתו מול קובנטרי, השחקן בן ה-23 מתכונן לרגע מרגש במיוחד כאשר אמו תגיע לצפות בו מהיציע לראשונה, בעוד אביו מלווה אותו באופן קבוע מאז המעבר מססואולו.  מוחארמוביץ' מייחס את הצלחתו להוריו, שנמלטו ממלחמת בוסניה ועברו לסלובניה ולאחר מכן לאוסטריה. לאחר תקופה בוולפסברגר האוסטרית ובמעבר ליובנטוס בגיל 18, שם התאמן תחת שחקנים כמו ג'ורג'ו קייליני ולונארדו בונוצ'י, הוא עבר לססואולו וזכה עמה באליפות סרייה ב'.  בקיץ האחרון בחר להגשים את חלומו ולעבור לפרמיירליג תחת המאמן דניאל פרקה. היכולת המרשימה של לידס לאחרונה מעוררת ציפיות גבוהות בקרב השחקנים והאוהדים לגבי אפשרות של העפלה למפעלים אירופיים, ומוחארמוביץ' מקווה להמשיך להוכיח את עצמו ברמה הגבוהה ביותר.
